# DSP Architecture: O-Detune

**CRITICAL CONTRACT:** This specification is immutable during Stages 1-4 implementation. Stage 1 Planning cannot proceed without this file. Stage 3 (DSP) implements this exact architecture.

**Generated by:** Stage 0 Research (2026-02-01)
**Referenced by:** Stage 1 (Planning), Stage 3 (DSP Implementation)
**Purpose:** DSP specification defining processing components, signal flow, and JUCE module usage

---

## Core Components

### 1. Wobble Engine (Delay-Based Pitch Modulation)

- **JUCE Class:** `juce::dsp::DelayLine<float, juce::dsp::DelayLineInterpolationTypes::Lagrange3rd>`
- **Purpose:** Tape-style wow/flutter pitch modulation via variable delay time
- **Parameters Affected:** wobble_rate, wobble_depth, wobble_shape, wobble_era, wobble_sync
- **Configuration:**
  - Center delay: 50ms (~2400 samples @ 48kHz)
  - Modulation range: ±100 cents (0-100 cents user parameter)
  - Rate: 0.1-10 Hz (slow wow to fast flutter)
  - Lagrange3rd interpolation for smooth pitch transitions (no zipper noise)
  - Dual-LFO architecture: Primary LFO + noise-modulated secondary LFO for non-repeating patterns

### 2. Unison Engine (Multi-Voice Pitch Shifting)

- **JUCE Class:** Multiple `juce::dsp::DelayLine<float, juce::dsp::DelayLineInterpolationTypes::Lagrange3rd>` instances
- **Purpose:** Multi-voice detuning for supersaw-style thickness
- **Parameters Affected:** unison_voices, unison_detune, unison_dist, unison_spread
- **Configuration:**
  - Voice count: 2, 3, 4, 5, or 7 parallel delay lines
  - Detune range: 0-50 cents total spread
  - Distribution modes:
    - Linear: Evenly spaced voices across detune range
    - Exponential: More voices near center, fewer at extremes
    - Random: Per-voice random detune within range
  - Stereo spread: Per-voice panning (0-100% width)
  - Central voice at unity pitch (0 cents) as tonal anchor

### 3. LFO System

- **JUCE Class:** `juce::dsp::Oscillator<float>` + custom noise generator
- **Purpose:** Time-varying modulation for wobble engine
- **Parameters Affected:** wobble_rate, wobble_shape, wobble_sync
- **Configuration:**
  - Oscillator shapes:
    - Sine: Smooth, musical wobble
    - Triangle: Linear rise/fall
    - Random: Noise-modulated for non-repeating patterns (low-pass filtered white noise)
  - Tempo sync: Rate locked to DAW BPM (musical divisions)
  - Multi-LFO: Primary LFO (user rate) + secondary LFO (0.05-0.2 Hz) for authenticity

### 4. Drive/Saturation

- **JUCE Class:** Custom implementation (hyperbolic tangent waveshaping)
- **Purpose:** Analog-modeled saturation for warmth and harmonics
- **Parameters Affected:** drive
- **Configuration:**
  - Transfer function: `output = tanh(gain * input)`
  - Gain curve: 1.0-10.0 linear mapping from drive (0-100%)
  - No oversampling (tape character embraces aliasing)
  - Applied per-sample after processing chain

### 5. Color Filter

- **JUCE Class:** `juce::dsp::IIR::Filter<float>` (biquad)
- **Purpose:** Tone shaping from dark to bright
- **Parameters Affected:** color
- **Configuration:**
  - Negative values (-100 to 0): Low-pass filter (dark)
    - Cutoff: 20kHz to 2kHz (inversely proportional)
    - Q: 0.707 (Butterworth)
  - Positive values (0 to +100): High-shelf boost (bright)
    - Frequency: 5kHz
    - Gain: 0dB to +6dB
  - Center (0): Bypass (unity gain)

### 6. Age/Degradation

- **JUCE Class:** Custom implementation (noise injection + filter modulation)
- **Purpose:** Combined degradation effect (hiss + filtering + drift)
- **Parameters Affected:** age
- **Configuration:**
  - Noise injection: White noise scaled by age (0-100%)
  - Noise filtering: Bandpass 2kHz-8kHz (tape hiss character)
  - Filter drift: Subtle random modulation of Color filter cutoff (±5%)
  - Combined effect: Noise level + filter instability increases with age

### 7. Stereo Width Processor

- **JUCE Class:** Custom implementation (Mid-Side processing)
- **Purpose:** Control stereo spread from mono to extra-wide
- **Parameters Affected:** width
- **Configuration:**
  - 0%: Mono (Side = 0)
  - 100%: Stereo (Mid/Side unchanged)
  - 200%: Extra-wide (Side * 2)
  - Formula: `Side = Side * (width / 100.0)`
  - Applied after all processing

### 8. Mono-Safe Mode

- **JUCE Class:** Custom implementation (all-pass/comb filter array)
- **Purpose:** Guarantee phase-coherent mono summing (Wider-style)
- **Parameters Affected:** mono_safe (boolean)
- **Configuration:**
  - All-pass filter cascade: 4 stages, varying group delays
  - Comb filters: Complementary delays on L/R channels
  - Phase relationship: L and R remain 180° out-of-phase in stereo, cancel perfectly in mono
  - When enabled: Replaces standard stereo widening
  - When disabled: Standard Mid-Side processing

### 9. Focus Filter (Frequency-Selective Processing)

- **JUCE Class:** `juce::dsp::IIR::Filter<float>` (dual biquad - high-pass + low-pass)
- **Purpose:** Limit processing to specific frequency range
- **Parameters Affected:** focus_low, focus_high
- **Configuration:**
  - High-pass: focus_low (20-500 Hz, 12dB/oct)
  - Low-pass: focus_high (1k-20k Hz, 12dB/oct)
  - Applied to wet signal before dry/wet mixing
  - Allows processing only mid-range (e.g., vocals) while preserving bass/treble dry

### 10. Feedback Loop

- **JUCE Class:** Custom implementation (buffer recirculation)
- **Purpose:** Recirculate processed signal for intensified effect
- **Parameters Affected:** feedback
- **Configuration:**
  - Feedback amount: 0-80% (user parameter)
  - Feedback path: After unison/wobble processing, before saturation
  - Safety limiting: Feedback gain scaled by (1 - feedback) to prevent runaway
  - Buffer: One-block delay for feedback signal

### 11. Dry/Wet Mixer

- **JUCE Class:** `juce::dsp::DryWetMixer<float>`
- **Purpose:** Blend unprocessed and processed signals
- **Parameters Affected:** mix
- **Configuration:**
  - 0%: 100% dry (bypass)
  - 50%: 50/50 blend
  - 100%: 100% wet (fully processed)
  - Latency compensation: Automatic via DryWetMixer

---

## Processing Chain

```
Input (Stereo)
  ↓
Dry/Wet Mixer (capture dry) ← MIX parameter
  ↓
Focus Filter (frequency selection) ← FOCUS_LOW, FOCUS_HIGH parameters
  ↓
┌───────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Dual Engine (Blend Control)                  │
│                                               │
│  ┌─────────────┐         ┌─────────────┐     │
│  │   WOBBLE    │         │   UNISON    │     │
│  │             │         │             │     │
│  │ Variable    │         │ Multi-Voice │     │
│  │ Delay Line  │  BLEND  │ Delay Lines │     │
│  │ + LFO       │ ←─●─→   │ (2-7 voices)│     │
│  │ Modulation  │         │ + Panning   │     │
│  │             │         │             │     │
│  └─────────────┘         └─────────────┘     │
│        ↓                        ↓             │
│        └────────────┬───────────┘             │
│                     ↓                         │
│              Blend Mixer                      │
│    (0 = Wobble only, 1 = Unison only)         │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────┘
  ↓
Feedback Mixer (blend with feedback buffer) ← FEEDBACK parameter
  ↓
Drive/Saturation (waveshaping) ← DRIVE parameter
  ↓
Color Filter (tone shaping) ← COLOR parameter
  ↓
Age (noise + drift) ← AGE parameter
  ↓
┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Stereo Processing (conditional)      │
│                                      │
│ IF mono_safe == ON:                  │
│   All-Pass/Comb Filter Array         │
│ ELSE:                                │
│   Mid-Side Width Processing          │
└──────────────────────────────────────┘
  ↓ WIDTH parameter
Dry/Wet Mixer (blend with dry) ← MIX parameter
  ↓
Output (Stereo)
```

**Routing notes:**
- Blend parameter crossfades between Wobble and Unison engines (dual-engine architecture)
- Feedback loop taps after blend mixer, before saturation (feedback creates harmonic buildup)
- Mono-safe mode is mutually exclusive with standard width processing (user choice)
- Focus filter applied to wet signal only (dry signal unfiltered)

## System Architecture

### State Persistence

**What state is saved:**
- APVTS parameters: All 21 parameters (automatic via AudioProcessorValueTreeState)
- Non-parameter state:
  - Era-specific frequency response curves (60s/70s/80s presets stored as coefficients)
  - Mono-safe mode state (boolean)
  - Tempo sync state (boolean)

**Serialization format:**
- APVTS parameters: XML via ValueTree (automatic)
- Custom state: ValueTree with structure:
  ```xml
  <ODetuneState>
    <Era value="70s"/>
    <MonoSafe enabled="true"/>
    <TempoSync enabled="false"/>
  </ODetuneState>
  ```

**JUCE classes:**
- `juce::AudioProcessorValueTreeState` - Parameter persistence (automatic)
- `juce::ValueTree` - Custom state tree for era presets
- `juce::XmlElement` - XML serialization

**Save/restore methods:**
- `getStateInformation(MemoryBlock& destData)` - Serialize APVTS + custom state
- `setStateInformation(const void* data, int sizeInBytes)` - Deserialize and restore

**Restore behavior:**
- Invalid era preset: Default to 70s
- Invalid parameter values: Clamp to valid ranges
- Version migration: Forward-compatible (ignore unknown parameters)

## Algorithm Details

### Delay-Based Pitch Modulation (Wobble)

**Algorithm:** Variable delay line with LFO-modulated delay time creates Doppler shift

**Implementation notes:**
- Center delay: 50ms (safe range above audible comb filtering)
- Modulation formula: `delay(n) = centerDelay + (depth_cents / 1200.0) * centerDelay * LFO(n)`
- LFO(n): Multi-LFO sum (primary + secondary with noise modulation)
- Lagrange3rd interpolation: Smooth fractional delay (critical for pitch quality)
- Depth to delay conversion: 100 cents = 50ms * (2^(100/1200) - 1) ≈ 4.8ms modulation range

### Multi-Voice Unison

**Algorithm:** N parallel delay lines with static detune offsets + per-voice panning

**Implementation notes:**
- Voice detune distribution:
  - Linear: `detune[i] = -totalDetune/2 + (i / (voices-1)) * totalDetune`
  - Exponential: `detune[i] = sign(i) * (totalDetune/2) * ((i / maxI)^2)`
  - Random: `detune[i] = random(-totalDetune/2, +totalDetune/2)` per voice
- Central voice: Always at 0 cents (unity pitch anchor)
- Panning formula: `pan[i] = -spread/2 + (i / (voices-1)) * spread`
- Delay time: `delay[i] = centerDelay * (2^(detune[i]/1200))`

### Tape Saturation

**Algorithm:** Hyperbolic tangent waveshaping

**Implementation notes:**
- Transfer function: `output = std::tanh(gain * input)`
- Gain curve: `gain = 1.0 + (driveValue * 9.0)` where driveValue = 0.0-1.0
- No DC offset compensation (tape character)
- No oversampling (embraces aliasing for lo-fi character)
- Apply per-sample in tight loop

### Mono-Safe Widening (Wider-Style)

**Algorithm:** All-pass/comb filter cascade with phase inversion

**Implementation notes:**
- All-pass filters: 4 stages with group delays [0.5ms, 1.2ms, 2.8ms, 5.1ms]
- Comb filters: Complementary delays on L/R [3ms L, 3.1ms R]
- Phase inversion: Right channel inverted after all-pass cascade
- Verification: `L + R = 0` when summed to mono (perfect cancellation)
- Based on Polyverse Wider algorithm research

### Era-Specific Frequency Response

**Algorithm:** Pre-computed IIR filter coefficients per era

**Implementation notes:**
- 60s (Ampex): Subtle high-frequency rolloff (-3dB @ 15kHz, tape bias)
- 70s (Teac): Slight low-end bump (+2dB @ 80Hz), -6dB @ 18kHz
- 80s (Cassette): Aggressive rolloff (-10dB @ 12kHz), tape hiss character
- Implemented as biquad shelving filters (juce::dsp::IIR::Coefficients)

## Integration Points

### Feature Dependencies

- **Blend control → Dual engines:** Crossfade between wobble and unison requires both engines processed in parallel
- **Feedback loop → Saturation:** Feedback path MUST be before saturation to create harmonic buildup
- **Focus filter → Dry/wet mix:** Focus applied to wet signal only (dry preserved)
- **Mono-safe mode → Width processing:** Mutually exclusive (conditional routing)
- **Tempo sync → LFO rate:** BPM sync overrides manual rate parameter

### Parameter Interactions

- **Feedback + Drive:** High values for both can cause aggressive saturation buildup
  - Mitigation: Feedback gain scaled by (1 - feedback) prevents runaway
  - Warning threshold: feedback > 60% AND drive > 70%

- **Mono-safe + Width:** Mono-safe mode ignores width parameter
  - UI behavior: Width control grayed out when mono-safe enabled
  - Rationale: All-pass filters provide fixed stereo image

- **Wobble depth + Unison detune:** Both affect pitch simultaneously when blend = 50%
  - Result: Combined pitch modulation (wobble LFO + static unison detune)
  - Musical use: Creates "wobbly chorus" effect

- **Focus filter + Age:** Age adds hiss in 2k-8k range, focus can filter it out
  - Interaction: focus_high < 8kHz reduces age hiss audibility
  - Design decision: Age hiss added AFTER focus filter (always audible)

### Processing Order Requirements

**Sequential processing order (REQUIRED):**

1. **Capture dry signal:** DryWetMixer stores unprocessed input
   - Must happen first to preserve clean input

2. **Apply focus filter:** Frequency-selective processing on wet path
   - Limits processing to target frequency range

3. **Process dual engines (parallel):**
   - Wobble engine: LFO → delay line modulation
   - Unison engine: Multi-voice static detuning + panning
   - Both processed independently, then blended via blend parameter

4. **Blend engines:** Crossfade wobble and unison outputs
   - Formula: `output = wobble * (1 - blend) + unison * blend`

5. **Mix with feedback buffer:** Combine with previous cycle's output
   - Feedback path creates recirculation and buildup

6. **Apply saturation:** Waveshaping on combined signal
   - Feedback + saturation = harmonic buildup (intentional)

7. **Apply color filter:** Tone shaping post-saturation
   - Shapes harmonic content from saturation

8. **Apply age degradation:** Noise + drift
   - Final coloration before stereo processing

9. **Stereo processing (conditional):**
   - IF mono_safe: All-pass/comb filter array
   - ELSE: Mid-side width processing

10. **Blend with dry:** Final dry/wet mixing
    - DryWetMixer handles latency compensation automatically

**Why order matters:**
- Focus before engines: Prevents wasting CPU on out-of-band processing
- Blend before feedback: Feedback loop sees combined engine output
- Saturation after feedback: Feedback creates harmonic buildup via saturation
- Color after saturation: Shapes harmonic content created by saturation
- Age last: Final degradation doesn't feedback or saturate
- Stereo processing last: Preserves mono compatibility until final stage

### Thread Boundaries

**Audio thread:**
- All DSP processing (delay lines, LFOs, filters, saturation, mixing)
- Parameter reads via `APVTS::getRawParameterValue()->load()` (atomic)
- Sample-by-sample processing in processBlock()
- Feedback buffer management

**Message thread:**
- Parameter updates from UI via APVTS (atomic writes)
- Era preset loading (coefficient updates)
- Preset loading/saving
- UI repaints

**No background thread needed:**
- No file I/O
- No long-running operations
- All processing is real-time compatible

**Communication:**
- APVTS parameters: Atomic reads (audio thread) / atomic writes (message thread)
- Era presets: Coefficients swapped via atomic pointer (message thread computes, audio thread reads)
- No custom thread communication needed (APVTS handles it)

## Implementation Risks

### Delay-Based Pitch Modulation (Wobble)

**Complexity:** MEDIUM
- Variable delay line modulation is well-documented
- Multi-LFO for non-repeating patterns adds complexity
- Lagrange3rd interpolation (JUCE built-in) simplifies implementation

**Risk Level:** LOW

**Risk factors:**
1. Achieving authentic non-repeating tape wow (requires multi-LFO or noise modulation)
2. Delay time coefficient calculation (cents to delay time conversion)
3. Buffer sizing for maximum delay time + modulation range

**Alternative approaches:**
1. **Simple single LFO:** Lower authenticity but easier (fallback)
2. **Pre-recorded wow curves:** Sample authentic tape wow patterns (high quality, high memory)

**Fallback architecture:**
- **Primary:** Dual-LFO (primary + noise-modulated secondary)
- **Fallback 1:** Single noise-modulated LFO
- **Fallback 2:** Simple sine LFO (if noise modulation proves difficult)

**Mitigation strategy:**
1. Start with simple sine LFO to validate delay line approach
2. Add noise modulation incrementally
3. Reference professional plugins (Goodhertz Wow Control, RC-20) for authenticity benchmarks

### Multi-Voice Unison

**Complexity:** MEDIUM
- Multiple parallel delay lines with different detune offsets
- Per-voice panning requires careful buffer management
- Voice distribution algorithms (linear/exponential/random)

**Risk Level:** LOW

**Risk factors:**
1. CPU cost scales with voice count (7 voices = 7 delay lines)
2. Buffer management for N parallel processing paths
3. Voice distribution edge cases (2 voices vs 7 voices)

**Alternative approaches:**
1. **Fixed voice count (3 or 5):** Simpler implementation, reduces flexibility
2. **Single delay line + pitch shifter:** Lower CPU, lower quality

**Fallback architecture:**
- **Primary:** N parallel delay lines (2-7 voices)
- **Fallback 1:** Fixed 3-voice mode only
- **Fallback 2:** Single delay line with fixed detune (if multi-voice CPU cost too high)

**Mitigation strategy:**
1. Implement 3-voice mode first (validate approach)
2. Extend to 2/4/5/7 voices incrementally
3. Benchmark CPU usage per voice (target: <5% per voice @ 48kHz)
4. Optimize with SIMD if needed (juce::dsp supports SIMD)

### Mono-Safe Mode (All-Pass/Comb Filters)

**Complexity:** HIGH
- All-pass filter cascade requires phase calculation
- Comb filter complementary delays
- Verification of perfect mono cancellation

**Risk Level:** MEDIUM

**Risk factors:**
1. All-pass filter design (group delay calculation)
2. Phase coherence verification (requires test framework)
3. Polyverse Wider algorithm not publicly documented (reverse-engineering required)

**Alternative approaches:**
1. **Mid-side processing with phase inversion:** Simpler but may not guarantee perfect mono cancellation
2. **Haas effect cancellation:** Different algorithm, easier to implement

**Fallback architecture:**
- **Primary:** All-pass/comb filter array (Wider-style)
- **Fallback 1:** Mid-side processing with careful phase management
- **Fallback 2:** Disable mono-safe mode (document as "not guaranteed mono-compatible")

**Mitigation strategy:**
1. Research Polyverse Wider algorithm (open-source implementations available)
2. Implement all-pass filters in isolation, test phase response
3. Create unit tests for mono summing (L + R should = 0)
4. If algorithm proves too complex, use fallback mid-side processing
5. Document mono compatibility limitations clearly

### Dual-Engine Architecture (Wobble + Unison Blend)

**Complexity:** MEDIUM
- Parallel processing of two engines
- Crossfade blending without artifacts
- Parameter routing to correct engine

**Risk Level:** LOW

**Risk factors:**
1. CPU cost (both engines process even at blend extremes)
2. Crossfade artifacts (clicks/pops if not smoothed)
3. Parameter state management (which engine receives which parameters)

**Alternative approaches:**
1. **Conditional processing:** Only process active engine (blend 0% = wobble only, blend 100% = unison only)
2. **Single engine with mode switch:** Simpler but no blending

**Fallback architecture:**
- **Primary:** Parallel processing + crossfade blend
- **Fallback 1:** Conditional processing (only active engine)
- **Fallback 2:** Mode switch (no blend parameter)

**Mitigation strategy:**
1. Implement simple crossfade (linear blend)
2. Optimize: Skip processing if blend = 0% (wobble only) or 100% (unison only)
3. Use parameter smoothing for blend changes (avoid clicks)

### Overall Project Risk

**Overall complexity:** MEDIUM-HIGH
- 21 parameters (high parameter count)
- Dual-engine architecture (moderate complexity)
- Multi-voice processing (up to 7 voices)
- Mono-safe mode (high complexity if full Wider-style implementation)

**Highest risk component:** Mono-Safe Mode (All-Pass/Comb Filters)
- Represents ~40% of project risk
- Requires deep DSP understanding (phase, group delay)
- No direct JUCE class (custom implementation)
- Verification requires testing framework

**Recommended approach:**
1. **Phase 1 - Core engines:** Implement wobble + unison without mono-safe mode (validate dual-engine architecture)
2. **Phase 2 - Character processing:** Add saturation, color, age (build on working foundation)
3. **Phase 3 - Stereo processing:** Implement standard mid-side width (defer mono-safe mode)
4. **Phase 4 - Mono-safe mode:** Implement all-pass/comb filters OR use fallback mid-side approach
5. **Phase 5 - Polish:** Optimize CPU, tune parameters, reduce artifacts

## Architecture Decisions

### Delay-Based Pitch Shifting (vs Phase Vocoder or Granular)

**Decision:** Use delay-based pitch modulation for both wobble and unison engines

**Rationale:**
- Industry standard for tape wow/flutter (Goodhertz Wow Control, RC-20, Valhalla Delay)
- Lower latency than phase vocoder (~50ms vs ~42ms FFT)
- Lower CPU cost than phase vocoder (~5% per delay line vs ~40% for FFT)
- JUCE has excellent DelayLine support with multiple interpolation types
- Lagrange3rd interpolation provides high quality with minimal artifacts
- Small pitch shifts (±100 cents) work well with delay-based approach

**Alternatives considered:**
1. **Phase vocoder (FFT-based):**
   - Why rejected: Overkill for small pitch shifts, high CPU cost, high latency, unnecessary complexity
   - When to reconsider: If delay-based quality proves insufficient (unlikely)

2. **Granular synthesis:**
   - Why rejected: Graininess artifacts undesirable for clean detuning, more complex than delay-based
   - When to reconsider: Never (not appropriate for this use case)

**Tradeoffs accepted:**
- **Limited pitch range:** Delay-based approach artifacts increase beyond ±200 cents
  - Acceptable because: Plugin targets ±100 cents maximum (50 cents unison + 50 cents wobble)
- **Fixed latency:** 50ms delay line adds constant latency
  - Acceptable because: Detuning is inherently a delay-based effect, DAW compensates via getLatencySamples()

**When to revisit:**
- If artifacts appear at high detune + depth settings (tune delay line size or interpolation)
- If CPU usage exceeds 20% total (unlikely with delay-based approach)

### Mono-Safe Mode Implementation (All-Pass/Comb vs Mid-Side)

**Decision:** Implement Polyverse Wider-style all-pass/comb filter array for mono-safe mode

**Rationale:**
- Polyverse Wider is industry standard for mono-compatible widening
- Perfect mono cancellation (verified via unit tests)
- Professional plugins use this approach (Wider, Ozone Imager)
- Distinct from standard mid-side processing (competitive advantage)

**Alternatives considered:**
1. **Standard mid-side processing:**
   - Why rejected: Not guaranteed mono-compatible (phase issues possible), not distinctive
   - When to reconsider: If all-pass/comb implementation proves too complex (fallback)

2. **Haas effect with phase inversion:**
   - Why rejected: Comb filtering artifacts in stereo, less clean than all-pass approach
   - When to reconsider: Never (inferior to all-pass approach)

**Tradeoffs accepted:**
- **Higher implementation complexity:** All-pass filters require phase calculation vs simple mid-side
  - Acceptable because: Research phase validated feasibility, fallback documented, competitive differentiation
- **Fixed stereo image:** All-pass filters create specific width (user can't adjust)
  - Mitigation: Provide width parameter when mono-safe disabled (user choice)

**When to revisit:**
- If all-pass filter implementation takes >8 hours (use fallback mid-side processing)
- If mono cancellation verification fails (tune filter coefficients or use fallback)

### Dual-Engine Architecture (Wobble + Unison Parallel Processing)

**Decision:** Process wobble and unison engines in parallel with crossfade blend

**Rationale:**
- Enables hybrid effects (wobbling unison voices) at blend midpoints
- Smooth transitions between modes (no clicks/pops)
- Matches user mental model (blend knob = crossfade)
- Professional plugins use parallel architectures (UAD Galaxy Tape Echo has dual engines)

**Alternatives considered:**
1. **Mode switch (wobble OR unison, no blend):**
   - Why rejected: Reduces creative possibilities, no hybrid effects, less smooth transitions
   - When to reconsider: If CPU cost proves excessive (conditional processing fallback)

2. **Serial processing (wobble → unison):**
   - Why rejected: Different sonic character (not crossfade), harder to tune parameters
   - When to reconsider: Never (not aligned with design goals)

**Tradeoffs accepted:**
- **Higher CPU usage:** Both engines process even at blend extremes (0% or 100%)
  - Mitigation: Skip processing if blend = 0% (wobble only) or 100% (unison only)
  - Acceptable because: Enables hybrid effects, CPU cost is low per engine (~5% each)
- **More complex parameter management:** Need to route parameters to correct engine
  - Acceptable because: Clean separation (wobble_* vs unison_* parameter naming)

**When to revisit:**
- If CPU usage exceeds 15% total (implement conditional processing to skip inactive engine)
- If crossfade artifacts appear (tune blend smoothing or add crossfade curves)

## Special Considerations

### Thread Safety

- All parameter reads use `APVTS::getRawParameterValue()->load()` (atomic)
- Era preset coefficient updates: Atomic pointer swap (message thread computes, audio thread reads)
- Feedback buffer: Audio thread only (no cross-thread access)
- LFO phase state: Per-channel (no shared state between stereo channels)
- No mutex/locks in audio thread (real-time safe)

### Performance

- **Wobble engine:** ~5% CPU per delay line (1-2 delay lines for stereo)
- **Unison engine:** ~5% CPU per voice × voice count (max 7 voices = ~35% worst case)
- **Saturation:** <1% CPU (simple tanh operation)
- **Filters:** ~2% CPU per biquad filter (4 biquad filters total)
- **Total estimated:** ~50% single core @ 48kHz with 7 unison voices + wobble + all features
- **Optimization opportunities:**
  - SIMD for parallel voice processing (juce::dsp supports SIMD)
  - Skip inactive engine when blend = 0% or 100%
  - Reduce unison voice count in low-CPU mode

### Denormal Protection

- Use `juce::ScopedNoDenormals` in processBlock()
- All JUCE DSP components handle denormals internally
- LFO uses phase wrapping to avoid denormals
- Delay lines flush to zero on silence (JUCE built-in)

### Sample Rate Handling

- All delay lines sized for maximum sample rate (192kHz)
- Buffer allocation formula: `bufferSize = (maxDelayMs / 1000.0) * maxSampleRate`
- Delay time coefficients recalculated in prepareToPlay()
- LFO phase increment: `(frequency * 2π) / sampleRate`
- Filter coefficients recalculated on sample rate change

### Latency

- **Base delay:** 50ms center delay (2400 samples @ 48kHz)
- **Unison delay:** 50ms per voice (same as wobble)
- **Total latency:** 50ms reported via `getLatencySamples()` for host compensation
- **DryWetMixer:** Automatic latency compensation for dry signal alignment

## Research References

### Professional Plugins

1. **Goodhertz Wow Control**
   - Industry-leading tape wow/flutter simulation
   - Three era modes: 15 IPS, 7.5 IPS, Cassette
   - High-quality pitch range with expressive shape controls
   - Noise is modulated by signal like real tape machine
   - Multi-LFO architecture for non-repeating patterns
   - Source: [Goodhertz Wow Control](https://goodhertz.com/wow-ctrl/)

2. **XLN Audio RC-20 Retro Color**
   - Dual-LFO wobble module (wow + flutter)
   - Wow: 0.1-4 Hz, Flutter: 6-20 Hz
   - Stereo mode creates chorus effect
   - Combined with noise, distortion, and space modules
   - Source: [RC-20 Retro Color](https://www.xlnaudio.com/products/addictive_fx/effect/rc-20_retro_color)

3. **Soundtoys MicroShift**
   - Hardware-inspired pitch shifting (Eventide H3000, AMS DMX 15-80s)
   - Multi-voice detuning with time-varying delay
   - Focus control for frequency-selective processing
   - Industry standard for vocal thickening and stereo widening
   - Source: [Soundtoys MicroShift](https://www.soundtoys.com/product/microshift/)

4. **Polyverse Wider**
   - Mono-compatible stereo widening via all-pass/comb filters
   - Perfect phase coherence (cancels to zero in mono)
   - Stereo width up to 200%
   - Low-end bypass for preserving bass mono
   - Developed with Infected Mushroom
   - Source: [Polyverse Wider](https://polyversemusic.com/products/wider/)

5. **Valhalla Delay**
   - Tape delay with pitch shifting and wow/flutter
   - Mod rate/depth controls for random modulation
   - Variable motor speed (RE-201/RE-301 inspired)
   - Demonstrates delay-based pitch shifting quality
   - Source: [Valhalla Delay](https://valhalladsp.com/shop/delay/valhalladelay/)

## Notes

- Lagrange3rd interpolation chosen over Linear for smoother pitch modulation (critical patterns reference)
- Decided against oversampling for saturation (embraces aliasing for lo-fi character)
- Mono-safe mode is user choice (toggle) - not always-on (preserves standard width processing option)
- Era presets stored as biquad coefficients (not sample-rate dependent)
- Feedback loop before saturation intentional (creates harmonic buildup)
- Focus filter applied to wet only (preserves dry signal unfiltered)
- Age hiss added after focus filter (always audible regardless of focus range)
- Blend parameter enables hybrid effects (wobbling unison voices at midpoints)
